Daily Digest · Computer Science

AI Agents Evolve: Tools, Trust, and Real Robots

Today's submissions reveal a maturing ecosystem where language model agents venture beyond text into physical and tool-rich environments. The dominant theme centers on securing LLM-tool boundaries, adapting pre-trained policies to novel scenes, and grounding abstract reasoning in multimodal perception. What's striking: researchers are solving the hard problem of making agents reliable when deploying them to real robots and users' homes—moving from lab benchmarks to genuine deployment constraints.

⚡ Highlighted Findings 4 selected · AI-curated
AI Safety
Securing LLM Tool Calls via Semantic Fuzzing Framework

ToFu automatically derives security checks for external tools that LLM agents invoke, addressing the gap where orchestrators may misinterpret model outputs. This matters because agents interacting with real systems—databases, APIs, robots—need guardrails beyond model alignment.

ToFu discovers semantic violations in LLM tool invocations that traditional input validation misses by leveraging CWE-guided sanitizer patterns.
Islam Ananto, Prevost-Avenel, Kim et al. 2610.13651 PDF
Robotics
Personalizing Robot Policies from Phone Scans Alone

Splat2Act bridges the gap between generalist manipulation models and real home environments by converting phone scans and object photos into sim-to-real adaptations. Users can now deploy pre-trained policies to unfamiliar scenes without collecting expensive real-world demonstrations.

A pretrained VLA achieving 0% success in unseen home scenes reaches functional performance through scene-specific adaptation from captured 3D data and object images.
Ye, Jaganathan, Lim et al. 2610.13945 PDF
Computer Vision
Identity Privacy Protection via Imperceptible Video Perturbations

KVeil won ECCV 2026's LifeGenIP Challenge by degrading facial video reference information while staying imperceptible, blocking personalized video generation attacks. As deepfakes threaten identity safety, this represents a practical defense mechanism scalable to real deployments.

Reference Capacity Collapse losses render facial videos unsuitable for identity cloning while preserving visual quality below human perceptibility thresholds.
Li, Xing, Li et al. 2610.13732 PDF
Machine Learning
Flow Matching Unifies Diffusion and Inverse Problem Solving

β-Flow provides a single plug-and-play framework generalizing over flow-matching and diffusion priors for linear inverse problems, with tunable correlation and confidence parameters. This resolves brittleness in prior methods that required bespoke approaches per model class.

Exact Gaussian conditioning on flow trajectories enables a unified posterior sampling method indexed by correlation parameter β that recovers both flow and diffusion limits.
Deveney, Bogensperger, Wong 2610.13812 PDF

Featured Researcher
SL
Shuran Song
Robotics Researcher · Columbia University

Shuran Song directs research in robot learning, focusing on bridging simulation and real-world manipulation through vision and language. Her lab has pioneered VLA-based approaches for generalizable robotic control, recently culminating in practical methods like Chronos Policy that make physical time explicit in robot decision-making. Featured today for advancing deployment-ready robotic agents that adapt to real homes and users.
